documenters-network.name: City Bureau Documenters Network
documenters-network.place: Chicago, Detroit, Cleveland, Minneapolis and other cities
documenters-network.outcome: Trains and pays residents to take notes at public meetings; all sites pay more than $15 an hour, Minneapolis $20
documenters-network.limits: Pay figures are from a 2022 article; current rates vary by city and are not listed on the network site.
documenters-network.locator: "All sites pay more than $15 per hour"

documenters-sites.name: Documenters local programs list
documenters-sites.outcome: About two dozen active local programs, from Akron to Wichita, with several more in hibernation
documenters-sites.limits: Self-described by the network; some sites are paused, and most are in metro areas.

signal-cleveland-documenters.name: Signal Cleveland Documenters
signal-cleveland-documenters.outcome: More than 1,400 public meetings covered in five years, informing more than 700 news stories
signal-cleveland-documenters.limits: Self-reported by the host newsroom; one city with foundation funding.

nj-documenters.name: New Jersey Documenters
nj-documenters.outcome: State-created consortium partnered with City Bureau to pay residents $20 an hour to document local meetings; aimed to train 200 in year one
nj-documenters.limits: Announcement only; the network site now lists some New Jersey sites as in hibernation.
nj-documenters.locator: Documenters earn $20 per hour for their time

nj-consortium.name: New Jersey Civic Information Consortium
nj-consortium.outcome: Created by the state in 2018; first round of 14 grants up to $35,000 from $500,000 in state funding
nj-consortium.limits: State funding has varied year to year; grants are small compared with lost newsroom budgets.
nj-consortium.locator: "Created by the state of New Jersey in 2018"

nj-organizing.name: Free Press News Voices organizing for the New Jersey consortium
nj-organizing.outcome: A coalition of residents, universities and journalists organized from 2017 to win the state law
nj-organizing.limits: Account from the advocacy group that led the campaign.

illinois-tax-credit.name: Illinois Local Journalism Sustainability tax credit
illinois-tax-credit.outcome: First year: more than $4 million in credits supporting more than 260 local journalist jobs at 55 news organizations; over half of the funding went outside the Chicago metro area
illinois-tax-credit.limits: First-year data from an advocacy group that helped design the law; only $260,000 of the $1 million for new hires was claimed, about three quarters unused.
illinois-tax-credit.locator: Over half of the funding went outside the Chicago metro area

washington-fellowship.name: Washington local journalism fellowship at WSU Murrow College
washington-fellowship.outcome: $2.4 million over two years to place eight recent graduates a year in local newsrooms for two-year stints
washington-fellowship.limits: Modeled on California's program; later reporting says the legislature cut its funding in 2025.
washington-fellowship.locator: "modeled after the California Local News Fellowship"

report-for-america.name: Report for America
report-for-america.outcome: Placed 107 new reporters in 101 local newsrooms; pays a large share of salary for up to three years while newsrooms raise the rest
report-for-america.limits: Newsrooms must raise matching money locally, and the program covers only a few hundred reporters nationally.
report-for-america.locator: "placing 107 journalists in newsrooms across the country"

outlier-media.name: Outlier Media TXT OUTLIER
outlier-media.outcome: Nonprofit newsroom answers residents' questions about eviction, property taxes and utility shutoffs by text message (text DETROIT to 67485); users can also talk to a reporter one-on-one; says it lets the community decide what it covers
outlier-media.limits: One city, donor-funded; serves Detroit only.

medill-news-deserts.name: Medill State of Local News 2025
medill-news-deserts.outcome: 213 counties with no local news source; about 50 million Americans with limited or no local news; more than 300 startups in five years
medill-news-deserts.limits: County-level counts; a county with one source may still have little coverage of a given town.
medill-news-deserts.locator: "The number of news desert counties rose to 213 in 2025"

medill-maps.name: Medill local news maps
medill-maps.outcome: National and state maps of local news sources by county
medill-maps.limits: Page did not confirm a search-by-county tool; maps are counts, not quality.
medill-maps.locator: "Explore the local news landscape through national and state level maps"

front-porch-forum.name: Front Porch Forum
front-porch-forum.outcome: Neighborhood email forums now available in all 251 Vermont towns; a forum works once 100 residents join
front-porch-forum.limits: Member figures are from an undated statewide expansion article; Vermont is small and rural.

councilmatic.name: Councilmatic
councilmatic.outcome: Open-source site to search 70,000+ Chicago City Council bills and follow committee meetings
councilmatic.limits: Covers a few places; the code is open source but someone local has to set it up.

agenda-watch.name: Agenda Watch (Big Local News and Reynolds Journalism Institute)
agenda-watch.outcome: Collects local government meeting documents daily so journalists can search them
agenda-watch.limits: Access limited to MuckRock users at verified organizations; regional coverage.
agenda-watch.locator: "automatically granted to MuckRock users affiliated with a verified organization"

usa-legal-notice.name: USA Legal Notice public notice search
usa-legal-notice.outcome: Searches public notices (hearings, ordinances, foreclosures) aggregated by state newspaper associations
usa-legal-notice.limits: Run with newspaper associations; coverage varies by state.
usa-legal-notice.locator: "Search notices that were originally published in U.S. newspapers"

notice-bills.name: State bills moving public notices to government websites
notice-bills.outcome: Several states weighed letting local governments post notices on their own websites instead of newspapers
notice-bills.limits: Written by a newspaper industry foundation that opposes the change; outcomes of each bill not confirmed.
notice-bills.locator: "part of the three-legged stool of government accountability"

google-alerts.name: Google Alerts
google-alerts.outcome: Free email alerts when new search results match a topic, such as a town name
google-alerts.limits: Catches only what is published online; a news desert produces few results.
google-alerts.locator: "You'll get emails whenever we find matching search results"

cascadia-meetings.name: Cascadia Daily News public meetings guide
cascadia-meetings.outcome: Local newsroom keeps a dashboard of city, county and school board meetings with agendas and recordings
cascadia-meetings.limits: One region's newsroom; most places have no such dashboard.
cascadia-meetings.locator: "meetings you may not have known were public"

plural-legislators.name: Plural Open (formerly Open States) legislator lookup
plural-legislators.outcome: Free address lookup for state legislators plus open legislative data and an API
plural-legislators.limits: State legislators only, not city or county officials; API terms set by Plural.
plural-legislators.locator: "the biggest collection of open legislative data"

inn-index.name: Institute for Nonprofit News Index 2026
inn-index.outcome: 412 nonprofit newsrooms reporting; more than $750 million combined revenue in 2025
inn-index.limits: Page returned 403; figures from search summary only.

brown-act-agendas.name: California Brown Act 72-hour agenda rule
brown-act-agendas.outcome: Local bodies must post agendas at least 72 hours before regular meetings, including online
brown-act-agendas.limits: Official code page returned 403; seen only in bill text summaries.
